opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Martin (employee ID E033) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E033.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Employee is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin to Payroll, but admin is only allowed when the employee's role owns the system; Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist. Granting max allowed level of write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB records E033 as a contractor with basic security training (note from prior memory saying full-time appears inaccurate per Security DB). Contractors with basic training are limited to read; admin is never allowed for contractors. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Jennifer Martin (E033) requested admin to Payroll. Security DB records her as a contractor with basic security training, indicating the earlier full-time note is inaccurate. Per policy, contractors with basic training are limited to read, and admin is never allowed for contractors. The requested admin level exceeds the maximum of read, so the maximum permitted level (read) is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket carefully.

The employee Jennifer Martin (E033) requests admin access to Payroll.

Two notes in team memory:
- Note 1: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation for Payroll: write. Comment says full-time Analyst, requested admin, admin only allowed when role owns system; Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist. Grant write.
- Note 2: role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training: basic, recommendation: read. Comment says Security DB records E033 as contractor with basic security training, prior memory noting full-time appears inaccurate per Security DB. Contractors with basic training limited to read; admin never allowed. Recommend read.

Conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. As the Approver, I need to make a decision. The security DB note says the full-time info appears inaccurate per Security DB. Hmm.

Access policy:
- full_time: up to write; admin only if role owns the system. Analyst doesn't own Payroll (Payroll Specialist owns it). So max for full-time Analyst = write. Requested admin > write → grant write.
- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Security training basic → max read. Requested admin > read → grant read.

Which employment type applies? The two notes disagree. Note 2 explicitly says Security DB records E033 as contractor and that the prior full-time note appears inaccurate. Security DB is likely more authoritative for access decisions. Also note 2's comment directly addresses the discrepancy.

Given the security DB indicates contractor with basic training, the max is read. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.

Actually, let me think. The HR note (note 1) says full-time. Security note (note 2) says contractor and explicitly flags the HR record as inaccurate. The security team's data is typically authoritative for access. I'll grant read.

I'll submit decision with level read and reasoning.
